radiology_report:
Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate
Facility: Spaarne Gasthuis, Haarlem
Date: 28 Jan 2025

Clinical Indication: Prostate cancer screening re-evaluation. PSA 0.44 ng/mL, prior negative biopsy.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume: 29.0 mL. Zonal anatomy remains normal. A 6 mm focus occupies the right mid-gland peripheral zone. T2-weighted sequences show iso- to mildly hypointense signal compared to adjacent peripheral tissue. Diffusion-weighted imaging reveals mild restriction lacking definitive ADC correlation. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences demonstrate neither early nor progressive enhancement. Seminal vesicles appear unremarkable. There is no evidence of extraprostatic extension or suspicious lymphadenopathy.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 3 lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone. PSAD 0.03 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.57961565.

previous_notes.author: Dr. C. Peters (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial prostate cancer risk assessment continues following first-line PSA screening. A March 2024 repeat test showed a stable PSA of 0.4 ng/mL alongside an absence of acute urinary complaints or digital rectal irregularities. The ongoing clinical question, combined with the patient's desire for definitive risk stratification, led to a urology scheduling for specialist re-evaluation.
